newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia's Howard eyes taxation reform.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia's Howard eyes taxation reform.

text.p: Australian prime minister John Howard said on Friday that he was interested in taxation reform, but that his government remained committed to not introducing a goods and services tax (GST) in its current three year term.
"I think we have a less than perfect taxation system," Howard told a luncheon of the Committee for Economic Development of Australia (CEDA).
"Let me assure you I have not lost interest in the cause of taxation reform, but I made a committment and I will adhere to that commitment in relation to this term," he said.
Howard said, however, that he was wary of those commentators who promoted the cause of a GST as a solution for all of the Australian economy's problems.
He also said his Liberal-National Coalition had campaigned for a GST at the 1993 election and the public had decisively rejected that proposal.
Those who believed that a community consensus had now formed in favour of a GST may have been premature because a specific proposal had yet to be made and opposition to a GST had yet to resurface.
The the then Labour government campaigned strongly against a GST in the 1993 election and the proposal was subsequently dropped by the Coalition for the 1996 election.
Some opinion polls have recently shown renewed support for the idea of a GST and several prominent community groups have come in support of the new tax.
